tldr: On-device and browser-local AI gained notable new tooling: QVAC described a 0.8B assistant, PyTorch added a WebGPU inference path, and TNG explored modular MoE specialization; benchmark performance remains largely author-reported.

Google broadened Gemini 4 Carbon access while a new SVG-animation benchmark showed how executable graders can complement model judgments; Helsing's military-agent platform and renewed US–China AI dialogue warrant scrutiny of safety claims, oversight and real-world evidence.

news.title: QVAC introduces BotPsy, a sub-billion-parameter tool-use assistant
news.summary: QVAC published BotPsy, an approximately 0.8B-parameter model adapted from Qwen3.5-0.8B for on-device assistants and multi-step tool calls, with a multi-stage training procedure and author-run evaluations.
news.why_it_matters: Specialized small models can offer private, lower-resource tool use, making the approach relevant to local assistants instead of routing every interaction to frontier APIs.
news.caveat: Reported benchmark improvements are author evaluations, not independent replications; the paper acknowledges significant remaining safety weaknesses, including susceptibility to harmful instructions and prompt injection. Actual downloadable checkpoint terms and hardware performance require separate verification.

news.title: Helsing announces Clarity, a military multi-agent intelligence platform
news.summary: Helsing unveiled Clarity, an agent-based platform intended to join sensor streams, reports and other military data into an intelligence picture with human review in the decision workflow.
news.why_it_matters: It illustrates operational deployment ambitions for multi-agent information fusion and raises consequential questions about evidence quality, automation bias and human control in military settings.
news.caveat: Its performance and human-control safeguards are company descriptions; independent field validation and actual deployment coverage were not established. Do not confuse platform marketing with proven operational effectiveness.

news.title: Google expands Gemini 4 Carbon availability and agent tooling
news.summary: Google announced broader access to Gemini 4 Carbon through its developer and customer surfaces and described agent coordination through Antigravity's preview /swarm workflow.
news.why_it_matters: Developers evaluating long-context multimodal models and collaborative coding agents now have a newly described access and workflow option.
news.caveat: Availability, quota and billing vary by product and eligibility; Google benchmarks are vendor-reported and the coordination feature is preview, not a universally released stable API.

news.title: ExecuTorch gains a WebGPU path for local browser inference
news.summary: The PyTorch team documented an ExecuTorch WebGPU backend that runs exported PyTorch models as .pte files on supported browser GPUs, including examples spanning text, vision and speech.
news.why_it_matters: Direct browser-local GPU execution can preserve prompt data on a device and reduce dependency on cloud inference for compatible workloads.
news.caveat: Authors' speed comparisons against their selected CPU path are not cross-framework benchmarks. Model coverage, memory, WebGPU browser support and device-specific compatibility must be tested.

news.title: Figma and Stanford release an SVG animation benchmark with executable checks
news.summary: MotionGraphicsBench introduces 100 static-SVG-to-motion tasks graded with explicit executable verification programs; its researchers evaluated 32 model configurations and released benchmark resources.
news.why_it_matters: Task-specific programmatic graders can complement model-as-judge evaluation when outputs have properties that can be checked deterministically.
news.caveat: Authors report only four evaluated systems exceeded 50% pass@1 and a 93.3% raw grader-human agreement on a held-out sample; results and grader correctness are not independently reproduced, and grading tests can miss visual quality.

news.title: TNG explores adding independently trained specialists to MoE models
news.summary: TNG researchers describe training and integrating new domain-specific experts into an existing mixture-of-experts base model, with worked coding-domain experiments and comparisons against adapter fine-tuning.
news.why_it_matters: Modular domain adaptation could help small teams specialize an MoE model without retraining every existing expert or deploying separate full models.
news.caveat: The authors' evaluations are workload-specific; expert-router compatibility, quality tradeoffs and total memory requirements limit portability, and this is not a universal plug-and-play skill transfer result.

news.title: OpenAI opens beta business listings and scoped Business Agents in ChatGPT
news.summary: OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, including business-claimed information, aggregate discovery insights and Business Agents initially offered to eligible U.S. ecommerce and online-service businesses.
news.why_it_matters: The release creates a distinct business-to-user agent interaction surface with implications for discovery, attribution, trust and merchant data maintenance.
news.caveat: This is a restricted beta, not an account-wide public rollout. Availability, eligibility and data practices must be checked against product documentation; no independent outcome metrics were established.

news.title: Anthropic starts roadshow for a proposed public offering
news.summary: Anthropic launched a roadshow for a proposed stock offering with an indicated $70–$78 share-price range and a planned Nasdaq listing under ANT.
news.why_it_matters: A proposed listing could reshape public-market scrutiny of frontier-model economics, capital needs and governance.
news.caveat: This is a proposed, not completed, IPO. The company's statement says the registration statement had not yet become effective, so pricing, timing and completion remain uncertain.

news.title: OpenAI and Upwork report shifting demand for AI-related freelance work
news.summary: An OpenAI–Upwork analysis describes changes in posted freelance tasks, combinations of requested skills and larger project budgets among AI-related work on the platform.
news.why_it_matters: It supplies a concrete platform-level signal about how businesses are restructuring some contracted work around AI.
news.caveat: The sample represents Upwork postings, not the whole labor market; associations cannot establish that AI caused the reported shifts, and the analysis involves the participating companies.

news.title: US and China discuss possible AI incident-alert and testing dialogue
news.summary: Reuters reports that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a clear-eyed approach to AI cooperation and competition and described potential discussions on model testing practices and incident alerts.
news.why_it_matters: Even preliminary international coordination about testing and incident reporting matters for cross-border AI safety governance.
news.caveat: Reported remarks and prospective talks do not constitute a binding agreement, functioning alert channel or adopted regulatory standard.

technologies.name: BotPsy 0.8B
technologies.explanation: A roughly 0.8B-parameter assistant derived from Qwen3.5-0.8B and post-trained through staged supervised, distillation and reinforcement methods for tool-calling and mobile-assistant workflows.
technologies.conditional_advantage: May handle narrow local app/tool tasks with substantially lower runtime footprint than server-hosted frontier models, subject to measured reliability.
best_fit_uses: Local tool-call research and constrained agent workflows
tradeoffs: Weaknesses in difficult multi-step retrieval and adversarial prompting
Task performance varies across tools, and no independent benchmark replication
alternatives: Cloud agents with explicit user controls
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Sub-billion-parameter transformer; actual RAM, quantization and battery requirements depend on device and runtime, not independently measured for all devices.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Public checkpoint and license conditions must be independently checked before integration.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Author announces research and points to model resources; deployment quality and platform support unverified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No universal deployment cost or hosted service price established.

technologies.name: ExecuTorch WebGPU backend
technologies.explanation: Runs torch.export-to-ExecuTorch .pte model artifacts on a browser GPU through a WebGPU compute backend, enabling on-device web inference.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Potentially reduces server latency and transmission of user data for supported browser/model combinations.
best_fit_uses: Offline-first vision and speech inference pages
tradeoffs: GPU/browser support and memory ceilings vary
Operator coverage and runtime bundling need testing
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: WebGPU-capable browser and compatible GPU drivers; memory and operator support depend on model and device.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Project license likely follows ExecuTorch, but verify bundled backend and model licenses before use.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Backend documentation and playground available; production compatibility and browser rollouts vary.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Open tooling does not eliminate device and distribution costs; hosted inference is not required for local execution.

technologies.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
technologies.explanation: Google's newly announced frontier model offering for multimodal and long-context interactions, exposed through specified Google developer and customer products.
technologies.conditional_advantage: A single multimodal model API can simplify workflows needing large context and multiple input modalities when supported and appropriately budgeted.
tradeoffs: Provider access, quotas and policy limits
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Cloud access through Google's specified API and products; 1M context announced but rate limits, costs and modality availability differ by surface.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Proprietary hosted service; specific terms vary by surface.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Availability announced November 10; feature previews and tier restrictions remain.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Pricing and quotas vary by API/account and require live provider verification.

technologies.name: MotionGraphicsBench
technologies.explanation: A benchmark of 100 SVG animation-edit tasks with deterministic executable checking programs and human-judgment comparison.
technologies.conditional_advantage: For SVG and code-structured output, explicit task checks can produce more reproducible grading than unconstrained aesthetic model judging.
best_fit_uses: Research on programmatic versus model-based graders
tradeoffs: Passing checks does not guarantee pleasing motion or general visual quality
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: SVG rendering and validation scripts plus candidate model inference; GPU needs depend on the tested model rather than the benchmark itself.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Dataset/code license must be checked on its repository before redistribution.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Public project, paper and dataset linked; versioned fixtures and current access should be rechecked.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Benchmark may be freely accessed, but model inference and human review can cost money.

technologies.name: Bring Your Own Expert MoE extension
technologies.explanation: A proposed method to train new domain-specific expert modules and integrate them with a pretrained mixture-of-experts model and its router, demonstrated on code domains.
technologies.conditional_advantage: For compatible MoE bases, domain-targeted capacity can be added without retraining every base expert.
best_fit_uses: Extending open MoE models with language-specific coding expertise
Comparing expert addition with LoRA on the same base
tradeoffs: Routing and interference can hurt general quality
Depends on MoE internals and training data
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Requires a compatible open MoE base with accessible expert architecture plus training compute and enough inference memory for the added experts.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Implementation and pretrained model licenses must be separately reviewed.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Research demonstration; a production-ready general expert plug-in interface is not established.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Custom expert training and serving cost depend on model, hardware and dataset.

terms.name: WebGPU browser inference
terms.definition: Running a machine-learning model inside a web browser while sending supported compute operations to the user's local GPU through the WebGPU API.
terms.mechanism: A model runtime translates supported operators to GPU compute workloads and handles model weights and tensors locally within browser/device limits.
terms.example: A browser page loads an exported .pte model and executes speech transcription on the device's GPU without submitting the audio to a remote inference server.
terms.caveat: Local execution does not automatically mean no network telemetry or complete privacy; app code, browser capabilities, model downloads and device memory still matter.

terms.name: MoE expert extension
terms.definition: Adapting a pretrained mixture-of-experts model by training and introducing additional specialized expert modules, rather than only updating its existing parameters.
terms.mechanism: New expert parameters specialize on target-domain data and routing or integration logic determines when tokens invoke them alongside original experts.
terms.example: A coding MoE receives an independently trained Rust-focused expert and the routing is evaluated for domain improvements and regressions.
terms.caveat: Expert addition is not guaranteed to preserve general capability; exact router behavior and added serving-memory costs determine usefulness.

terms.name: Programmatic benchmark verification
terms.definition: Evaluating a model-produced artifact with explicit executable checks for defined success conditions instead of relying solely on a human or language-model judge.
terms.mechanism: For each task, a validator executes or inspects the artifact and tests constraints such as element positions, transitions or structural requirements, producing a reproducible result.
terms.example: For a requested SVG motion, a grading script tests that specified objects move along permitted trajectories and preserve key positions.
terms.caveat: Passing explicit assertions can miss aesthetics, usability and untested failure modes; weak graders invite specification gaming.
